title: Introduce Batch Journeys and Quant Cost Maps (cost orchestration tools)
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Add Batch Journeys (workload-aware batching presets) and Quant Cost Maps (model-precision cost/latency profiles) with a new CLI to apply safe default profiles and an opt-in canary rollout for Dedicated clusters.
description: Motivation: teams frequently ask for a way to pick batching and quantization defaults that are tuned to their workload without trial-and-error. This PR introduces two orthogonal primitives: 1) Batch Journeys — a small DSL and set of presets that express workload 'journeys' (cold-heavy, chat-short-turns, long-completion) and map them to batching/cache defaults; 2) Quant Cost Maps — compact artifacts that capture per-model precision variants (fp16/int8/8+4/4bit) and their expected cost/latency/quality tradeoffs under common sequence length percentiles. Together these enable automated profile selection in Redwood Optimize and a safe CLI/console path for Dedicated/Private users to adopt conservative cost-saving defaults. Changes: single-string description of the user-visible changes and the implementation: - new CLI command: redwood cost-orch apply-profile --profile <journey> --cluster <id> --dry-run - batch-journey presets under internal/config/batch_journeys/{chat,api,long}.yaml - quant cost maps generated from webrtc-style microbench runs under telemetry/quant_maps/*.json - runtime adapter that consumes journey + quant map and emits a prioritized list of runtime hints (batch_size, max_latency_per_token_ms, kvcache_policy, quant_profile) - lightweight simulator that validates chosen profile against recent traffic samples before applying (CLI dry-run uses this) - telemetry: new metrics (rwi.batch_hint_applied, rwi.quant_profile_selected, rwi.profile_simulated_econ_delta) - canary rollout: console flag and api to apply profiles to 1%/10%/100% of traffic with automated rollback if latency/SLA regressions exceed thresholds Backwards compatibility and safety: profiles are always advisory; runtime will never lower per-request latency SLOs below the configured route level. We ship safe fallbacks: if quantized model variant fails to load, runtime falls back to the pinned canonical variant. Implementation notes: - batch journey DSL is intentionally small (3 top-level keys: selector, hints, thresholds) to make authoring predictable - quant maps are normalized to 95th/50th token-latency buckets and a small quality delta estimate (BLEU/ROUGE-like proxies for applicable models) - CLI leverages the existing orchestration API and introduces an idempotent apply operation with conservative defaults Testing and validation performed: - unit tests for YAML parsing and quant map ingestion - e2e simulator tests with synthetic workloads - benchmark runs on a small Dedicated pool (d-2-gpu-smoke) for each quant profile - integration smoke for console rollout UI - manual canary on a single customer cluster (log sanitized) Rollout plan: 1) behind feature flag (opt-in) for 2 weeks; 2) internal canary on non-prod clusters; 3) 10% Dedicated customers; 4) GA. Related: ENG-5227 (profiling pipeline), PM-118 (product spec), SUP-987 (support request for safer defaults).

example_journey_yaml:
selector:
  route: '/generate'
  traffic_shape: chat-short
hints:
  batch_size: 8
  max_latency_per_token_ms: 12
  kvcache_policy: aggressive
thresholds:
  p95_latency_ms: 300
  fallback_to_tiny_batch: true
